summary: Discovery focused on embedding routing and rerank costs for Garnet Retail. Customer currently uses hybrid stack (Elastic + Pinecone). Key concerns: P95 tail latency for rerank, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, fanout and top-K for vector lookups, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fits their compliance and throughput needs. Agreed to run a benchmark pilot with sample logs; Redwood to provide perf template and pricing guidance.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-08-09 16:00 PDT — Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Garnet Retail), Olivia Brooks (Head of Search), Diego Marquez (ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I m Maya, AE at Redwood, and Ethan here is our SE, he'll run through the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Good, thanks. Busy end of quarter but excited to dig in, we re trying to decide where to run our embedding + rerank workload.
[00:19] Olivia Brooks: Yeah we re seeing variability with Pinecone on peak, and Elasticsearch still handles a lot of metadata searches but we re exploring a tighter rerank flow.
[00:28] Ethan Rivera: Cool. Can you give us a quick picture of traffic and SLOs? Even ballpark QPS and tail latency targets helps.
[00:36] Diego Marquez: Sure — for the customer-facing product we have about 600 qps of embedding lookups during peak (that includes vector fanout for topK=100), and about 180 RPS that lead to rerank scoring with a lightweight generative call for context. Our target P95 for the full roundtrip is ~150-200ms, but reality is often 300-500ms on peaks.
[01:02] Maya Chen: Got it. When you say fanout 100, is that per query or do you do sharded topK across partitions?
[01:10] Diego Marquez: Right now it's per query. We do a single topK 100 from Pinecone; we ve considered sharding but felt complexity tradeoffs.
[01:19] Ethan Rivera: Ok. On the Redwood side, we typically look at two knobs — where embeddings are stored/queried (vector DB) and where rerank generation happens. Hosting options: Hosted API (fast to start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem). Each has different latency and cost tradeoffs.
[01:35] Olivia Brooks: Our compliance team also wants audit logs and KMS integration — so private or dedicated would be preferable if performance matches.
[01:44] Maya Chen: Understood. For audit/KMS we can support Private with customer-managed KMS, and Dedicated has enterprise audit logs too. We'll include doc links.
[01:52] Samir Patel: One question — embedding dimensionality. We're using 1024 dims for model X, but team wonders if 512 would be almost as good and save storage and compute. Any guidance?
[02:03] Ethan Rivera: Short answer: depends on recall requirements. For product title matching, 512 often suffices; for semantic nuance you may need 768-1024. You also get latency and memory wins with 512 — smaller vectors mean higher cache hit rates and faster dot products on CPU-backed index. But quantization changes this calculus.
[02:22] Olivia Brooks: We d be open to quantization. Our main risk is lift in false positives hurting conversion.
[02:29] Diego Marquez: Also running into memory pressure on sharded nodes when embedding dims are high — our ops wants fewer shards.
[02:35] Ethan Rivera: That aligns. For high fanout (topK 100) the vector DB CPU/memory profile is dominant. Redwood's approach can help reduce rerank calls via smarter filtering: do a first-pass smaller topK at edge or cache and then rerank on a compact set.
[02:52] Maya Chen: Quick clarifying Q — are you streaming tokens to the reranker or doing full-generation calls?
[02:57] Diego Marquez: We do short-generation scoring calls, typically 80-150 tokens. Not streaming.
[03:04] Ethan Rivera: Ok that helps. If you want sub-200ms P95 for the rerank, Dedicated with pinned GPU capacity is often the reliable path; Hosted can be fine for early pilot but bursts may hit queuing. Private (VPC) introduces network hop latencies depending on region placement.
[03:20] Samir Patel: Can you quantify the expected P95 difference? Like Hosted vs Dedicated for similar model loads?
[03:26] Ethan Rivera: Roughly speaking, for medium-size models and steady throughput we see Hosted P95 around 150-400ms depending on queueing and batch windows; Dedicated with properly sized pools and warm KV cache can get P95 sub-120-150ms. But depends on batching strategy — larger batches improve throughput but increase tail latency.
[03:44] Olivia Brooks: We re sensitive to cost. Dedicated is more expensive but predictable. How do you recommend we size an initial Dedicated pool?
[03:52] Ethan Rivera: Start by mapping expected concurrent rerank calls. With 180 RPS and average generation 100 tokens, and assuming we want to keep QPS per GPU under X (we gave a bench number), you could start with N gpus — we will give you a sizing worksheet. For the vector DB side, reducing dim from 1024 to 512 could roughly halve memory footprint; better to test recall delta with holdout set.
[04:18] Samir Patel: On hybrid search — we want to preserve some Elasticsearch filters pre-rerank. Could Redwood's routing do that?
[04:25] Maya Chen: Yes — many customers run hybrid: structured filters in ES, vector fanout for candidates, then rerank. Redwood routing can orchestrate that and do automatic fallback to a cheaper embedding model if the primary model times out.
[04:38] Diego Marquez: Fallback is huge for us — we need graceful degradation when capacity is constrained. Does Redwood support model variants and automatic failover?
[04:46] Ethan Rivera: Yep. Policy-based routing supports model variants, region fallback, and reducing topK for degraded mode. We also have prefix KV caching to reduce repeated context cost for similar queries. Note that fallback to smaller embedding dims is more invasive since it changes vector space; more common is fallback to smaller model for rerank scoring or shorter candidate lists.
[05:06] Olivia Brooks: Any recommendations on fanout to keep acceptable P95 without sacrificing recall?
[05:12] Ethan Rivera: A common pattern: fanout 100 offline to measure recall and set rerank threshold; in prod do fanout 30-50 for low-latency use cases and rely on reranker confidence calibration. Also consider cascading: cheap model to narrow to 50, then rerank heavy scorer.
[05:30] Samir Patel: Sounds sensible. A few routing concerns — we re geographically distributed, EU and NA. Data residency is important. Private deployment would solve that, yes?
[05:38] Maya Chen: Private or Dedicated in region can satisfy residency. Private gives you customer VPC and on-prem options if audit/compliance requires it. Dedicated can be regionally pinned as well, with SLAs.
[05:48] Diego Marquez: About benchmarks — what data do you need from us to run a meaningful pilot?
[05:52] Ethan Rivera: Access to a sample of query logs (anonymized), a candidate set size and labels for eval, traffic distribution (QPS per region), and the SLOs. We ll run an embedding topK + rerank throughput test and a tail-latency stress test.
[06:08] Olivia Brooks: We have synthetic logs we can share, but will need to scrub PII. Diego will handle that.
[06:14] Samir Patel: Ok another vendor question — we re also evaluating Milvus and Weaviate. Any integration differences to note?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Redwood integrates with most vector DBs via standard ANN ops. Differences are operational: Milvus gives control over sharding, Weaviate has semantic modules. We typically recommend picking a vector DB that matches your ops comfort, but Redwood s routing abstracts that away so you can change the backend later.
[06:37] Diego Marquez: Good. On costs — can you ballpark token + embed costs for our expected monthly traffic?
[06:43] Maya Chen: We'll put together an estimated cost model in the perf matrix including per-token, embedding generation, and Dedicated reserved vs on-demand amortized. We'll include burst pricing.
[06:51] Olivia Brooks: Great. Any security questionnaires or SOC 2 docs we can get?
[06:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send SOC2, ISO docs, and the Private deployment security checklist.
[07:01] Samir Patel: Next steps recap?
[07:04] Maya Chen: Redwood to send benchmark template + perf matrix, Pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private, Security docs. Garnet to share scrubbed logs and target SLOs. Then schedule a technical deep-dive (Ethan + Diego) to scope the pilot.
[07:16] Diego Marquez: I'll upload logs by Friday.
[07:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:21] Olivia Brooks: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcription contains a few mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" possible in a few spots); speakers occasionally overlap; timestamps approximate.
